name: libquantum
desc: C library for the simulation of quantum mechanics
why: Simulates quantum registers and algorithms like Shor's on a classical machine, a real door into quantum computation.

brief.what_it_is: libquantum is a C library for simulating quantum mechanics, with its main focus on quantum computing. It provides a quantum register with basic gates such as Hadamard and Controlled-NOT, and measurements on single qubits or the whole register. It can also compute the time evolution of arbitrary Hamiltonians, including time-dependent ones, by numerical integration of the Schrödinger equation or by exact diagonalization. The homepage says it includes implementations of Shor's factoring algorithm and Grover's search algorithm. It is a library, not a command-line tool: brew reports no executables.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage says it started as a pure quantum computer simulator and that support for general quantum simulation was added later. Its stated aim is to let people run quantum algorithms and quantum mechanics simulations on ordinary classical hardware with high performance and low memory use.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage describes an implementation of a quantum register with an easy-to-use interface for gates and measurements. Time evolution uses fourth-order Runge-Kutta integration or exact diagonalization, with optimizations for sparse Hamiltonians. Decoherence support, a quantum error correction interface, and the density operator formalism are also listed as features.
brief.install_notes: The homepage says libquantum requires a C compiler with complex number support. It has been reported to work on GNU/Linux (the main development platform), FreeBSD, OpenBSD, NetBSD, Mac OS X, HP Tru64 UNIX, and AIX. I did not read the downloads or documentation pages, so build steps and any configuration are not covered here.
brief.standout: It is a long-running C library that covers both gate-model quantum computing and general open-system or Hamiltonian simulation in one codebase. Its homepage lists Shor's and Grover's algorithms as built in, and it was an official SPEC CPU2006 benchmark.
brief.status: quiet. The newest item on the homepage is the 2013-01-29 release of libquantum 1.1.1, before that a 2010 Rydberg simulator note and a 2008 release of 1.1.0 and 1.0.0. I did not check a repository or the downloads page for later commits, so there may be newer activity I could not see.
brief.caveats: Licensed under GPL version 3, so it is Free Software with copyleft terms. There are no command-line tools; you use it from C code. The homepage news is several years old. The homepage does not describe the build process or give a usage example. Brew's caveats field is empty.

libquantum is a C library for the simulation of quantum mechanics, with a special focus laid to quantum computing.
Implementations of Shor's factoring algorithm and Grover's search algorithm are included
fetch_log: http://www.libquantum.de/ - fetched OK; homepage text included features, requirements, news, and authors. I did not follow the Documentation or Downloads links because the homepage did not give their exact URLs and the homepage content was already substantive.

judge.reason: A relatively obscure C library that lets you explore both quantum algorithms and Hamiltonian dynamics on classical hardware opens a genuinely interesting rabbit hole.

entry.title: libquantum
entry.tldr: A C library that simulates quantum registers, gates and measurements on an ordinary computer, with Shor's and Grover's algorithms included.
entry.deeper_look:
libquantum is a C library for simulating quantum mechanics, with a special focus on quantum computing. It gives you a quantum register, basic gates such as Hadamard and Controlled-NOT, and measurement of a single qubit or the whole register. Beyond gate-model computing, it can compute the time evolution of arbitrary Hamiltonians, including time-dependent ones, by numerical integration of the Schrödinger equation or by exact diagonalization.

According to its homepage, it began as a pure quantum computer simulator, and general quantum simulation was added later. The stated aim is to run quantum algorithms and quantum mechanics simulations on ordinary classical hardware with high performance and low memory use. The homepage also lists decoherence support, a quantum error correction interface, and the density operator formalism.

The idea underneath is that a quantum computer can be modelled classically, at a cost that grows quickly with the number of qubits. Implementations of Shor's factoring algorithm and Grover's search algorithm are included, so you can read how those famous algorithms look as gates acting on a register. It was also used as an official SPEC CPU2006 benchmark.

This is a library, not a command-line tool. You write C against it. The project is old and quiet, so treat it as a readable, working reference rather than a modern framework.
entry.install:
brew install libquantum
# Library only, no executables. Needs a C compiler with complex number support to build programs against it.
entry.whats_unique: One long-running C codebase covers both gate-model quantum computing and general Hamiltonian and open-system simulation. Shor's and Grover's algorithms ship with it.
entry.caveats: It installs no commands, so you must write C to use it, and the homepage gives no usage example or build steps; the latest news there is from 2013.
